description: Revision 3 field DAQ fit-check prototype with two PETG lids, a keyed perimeter wall, an interchangeable sensor cassette on the narrow end opposite SP16, outer PCB envelope retention, a removable positive-groove central bridge and separate TPU sealing and damping details.
releaseRequirements: Measure the delivered 60 × 80 mm KY00012 and 120 × 80 mm PY boards, bare substrate thickness and free edge lands. Confirm that no solder, component lead or copper feature is loaded by the envelopes, central bridge grooves or damping pads.

Verify the central bridge assembly sequence: seat boards first, lower the bridge and slide +Y3 mm until the unloaded leaf engages. Confirm mechanical inner-edge groove capture without relying on lid pressure or pad friction. Remove the lid, lift the release leaf 0.9 mm, slide −Y3 mm and lift the bridge before withdrawing one board inward 9.5 mm. Test the populated boards for protruding solder and lead interference; bare-substrate motion does not qualify every assembled PCB. Check the positive lid reverse-stroke backup and repeated leaf release cycles.

Match the delivered SP16-5 and SP20-3/4 female panel connectors to their source-dimension library models. Default mounting profiles have two opposing flats: SP16 Ø16.5 / 15.3 mm flat-to-flat and SP20 Ø20.5 / 19.5 mm flat-to-flat. Check flange, retaining nut, panel thickness, connector gasket, internal solder-tail envelope and matching cable half before fabrication.

Print the fit coupon using the final PETG material and printer profile. Inspect sliding clearance, elephant-foot effects, PCB insertion and cassette removal before printing the enclosure. The coupon nut trap checks side insertion, roof capture and thread start only; its blind screw-tip well is not a full tightening fixture.

Use four M3 screws of the selected under-head length with the matching base nut-seat geometry and four side-loaded nuts retained by base-owned 3 mm bearing roofs. Add four steel flat washers 3.2 × 7 × 0.5 mm (ISO 7089 / DIN 125) seated on the PETG hard annuli. Fit the under-washer TPU seals (4.84 mm free OD / 2.8 mm free ID) and verify their 0.1 mm radial shaft interference and nominal 0.8 to 0.6 mm compression without making them the structural preload path. Check thread engagement, head seating, blind clearances, compression stops and repeated service cycles.

Verify the two lid gaskets, cassette U-seal, four board pads and four under-washer seals with the selected TPU hardness and print process. Inspect continuous contact, the overhanging reinforced lid, 1.35 × 1.2 mm perimeter gaskets in 2.0 × 0.96 mm glands, and the cassette stops that limit inward travel to 0.1 mm. Qualify the nominal 20% perimeter compression and 20–26.7% U-seal compression physically. No IP rating is assigned.

Route insulated wiring and strain relief outside the PCB clamp lands and closure hardware. Keep the connector bands clear of tall components and verify connector mating, nut tool access and cassette removal.

Test physical PETG and TPU prints, labels and connector seals on wet ground, in rain, snow and meltwater, including cold handling, realistic drops, soil contamination and repeated closure. Keep electronics out until these tests pass. R3 is a fit-check prototype; no IP or impact rating is assigned.
